Q: Can a web assembly be packaged as a Windows DLL? A:

Well, WebAssembly is executed by an engine. That may or may not be embedded in a browser. Some of the largest applications of Wasm today have nothing to do with browsers (or with JavaScript, for that matter). And it was intended that way.

Q: Math Rendering in SurveyJS (KaTeX or MathJax) A:

You can install the KaTeX library within your application and handle the survey.onAfterRenderQuestion or survey.onTextMarkdown function to process survey texts using the KaTeX library.

For more information and code samples, please refer to the following support threads:

  • Render Math with MathJax or KaTeX

  • How to use math expressions

Should you have any further questions, please let me know.

Q: How to sync Angular signals with AG Grid rowData without resetting unsaved in-grid changes? A:

The below line might be the problem, since it uses both map and new GridRow() to create new references of the array, so the updates are not going to the original reference (this.itemDetails()).

sortedLines = computed(() => {return this.productNoteLines()?.map(line => new GridRow(line)) ?? [];});

You can try initializing a new array when you initialize this.itemDetails() so that there is no need for sortedLines this will ensure updates are propagated to the original reference.

Q: What does the 'L' in the beginning even mean? A:

There are two types of window classes: WNDCLASSA and WNDCLASSW. The difference is that WNDCLASSA uses char strings, while WNDCLASSW uses wchar_t strings. However, you can use WNDCLASS, a macro that becomes WNDCLASSA or WNDCLASSW, depending on whether your project is "marked" as Unicode supportive (has #define _UNICODE and/or #define UNICODE). This marker can be in the included WinAPI headers.
